c2-gen-0027: On the fourth day God set lights in the firmament. Let's read Genesis 1:14.
c2-gen-0028: Eden's first river winds away from the garden, and Adam meets every creature God brings him. Let's look at Genesis 2:11 and 20 together.
c3-gen-0018: God divided the light from the darkness, and later Adam names his wife Eve. Let's read Genesis 1:4 and 3:20.
c3-isa-0017: Isaiah promises that the LORD will hear His own and that their labor will not be in vain. Let's turn to Isaiah 65:23 and 24.
c3-gen-0019: When God brought the woman to Adam, he spoke up with joy. Let's read Genesis 2:23 and 3:12.
c3-gen-0020: God set the lights in the firmament, and then Genesis sums up His finished work. Let's open Genesis 1:17 and 2:1.
c3-gen-0021: Genesis tells of the making of man, and later of the sorrow spoken to the woman. Let's read Genesis 1:27 and 3:16.
c3-gen-0022: Genesis shows God's design for marriage, and later Adam speaks of the woman God gave him. Let's dig into Genesis 2:24 and 3:12.
c3-rev-0006: John sees the holy city with its gates and its wall laid out before him. Let's read Revelation 21:15 and 26.
c3-rev-0007: Nothing that defiles shall ever enter the city. Let's look closely at Revelation 21:27 and 22:3.
c2-mrk-0010: After John was held under guard, Jesus came preaching and called people to repent. Let's read Mark 1:15.
c2-dan-0009: Daniel tells the king about the great image he saw in his dream. Let's turn to Daniel 2:31 and 37.
c3-dan-0007: Daniel explains the toes made partly of iron and partly of clay. Let's read Daniel 2:36 and 42.
c3-psa-0014: The psalmist pictures His mighty acts told from parents to children. Let's read Psalm 145:3 and 4.
c3-mat-0012: Great crowds gathered around Jesus by the sea, and later the disciples asked Him about the way He taught. Let's open Matthew 13:2 and 10.
c3-dan-0008: Daniel tells of a stone cut out of the mountain, not by any human work, that broke the metals in pieces. Let's read Daniel 2:45 and Psalm 145:1.
c3-dan-0009: God put the beasts and the birds under the king's rule, and Jesus came preaching after John was held under guard. Let's check Daniel 2:38 and Mark 1:14.
c3-mat-0013: Daniel speaks of a fourth kingdom that crushes all the others, and Jesus gives another picture of the kingdom of heaven. Let's read Matthew 13:47 and Daniel 2:40.
c3-psa-0015: Daniel speaks of kingdoms that rise and fall, and the psalmist sings of the LORD's own kingdom. Let's read Psalm 145:13 and Daniel 2:39.
c3-mat-0014: Jesus teaches the crowds, and the psalmist promises his mouth will speak the LORD's praise. Let's dig into Matthew 13:34 and Psalm 145:21.
c2-ezk-0014: The LORD promises to bring His scattered people back home. Let's read Ezekiel 36:24.
c2-jhn-0022: Jesus speaks of righteousness, because He goes to the Father. Let's read John 16:10 and 12.
c3-jhn-0011: Jesus speaks of the Helper and of the world's unbelief. Let's look at John 16:7 and 9 together.
c3-act-0007: Pentecost arrives, and Peter says this is what Joel spoke of. Let's read Acts 2:1 and 16.
c3-rom-0015: Paul says we were saved in this hope, and we eagerly wait with perseverance. Let's turn to Romans 8:24 and 25.
c3-jhn-0012: Jesus promises another Helper to abide with His disciples forever. Let's read John 14:16 and 16:14.
c3-act-0008: At Pentecost the crowd was amazed, and Peter says they are all witnesses. Let's open Acts 2:7 and 32.
c3-act-0009: Peter preaches Jesus at Pentecost, and the Lord added to the church daily. Let's read Acts 2:24 and 47.
c3-rom-0016: Paul says the creation was subjected to futility. Let's check Romans 8:8 and 20.
c3-gal-0003: Paul writes of the Spirit, and he warns against becoming conceited. Let's read Galatians 5:17 and 26.
c2-deu-0016: Moses passes on a promise from the LORD about a coming Prophet. Let's read Deuteronomy 18:18.
c2-exo-0023: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron while they were still in Egypt. Let's go to Exodus 12:1 and 2.
c3-lev-0005: Aaron dresses in holy linen and washes himself before he ministers. Let's read Leviticus 16:4 and 7.
c3-exo-0008: Every household takes a lamb, and they keep it until the fourteenth day. Let's look closely at Exodus 12:4 and 6.
c3-heb-0010: The priests always went into the first part of the tabernacle. Let's read Hebrews 9:1 and 6.
c3-lev-0006: That day is a sabbath of solemn rest. Let's turn to Leviticus 16:20 and 31.
c3-lev-0007: Aaron brings the bull's blood inside the veil, and the anointed priest serves in his father's place. Let's read Leviticus 16:14 and 32.
c3-gen-0023: Abraham and Isaac reach the place God had shown him, and later the LORD swears by Himself. Let's read Genesis 22:10 and 16.
c3-heb-0011: The high priest went in alone once a year, and never without blood. Let's check Hebrews 9:3 and 7.
c3-heb-0012: Hebrews walks us through the furnishings of the tabernacle. Let's read Hebrews 9:5 and 10.
c2-psa-0024: Psalm 22 describes those who see the speaker and mock Him. Let's read Psalm 22:7.
c2-isa-0025: Isaiah asks, "Who has believed our report?" Let's look at Isaiah 53:1 and 4 together.
c3-psa-0016: The psalmist begs God not to be far, for trouble is near. Let's read Psalm 22:1 and 11.
c3-isa-0018: Isaiah says the righteous Servant shall justify many. Let's open Isaiah 53:8 and 11.
c3-jhn-0013: At the cross the soldiers took His garments, and later He was offered sour wine. Let's read John 19:23 and 29.
c3-psa-0017: The psalmist says the wicked have enclosed Him, and John points to another Scripture fulfilled at the cross. Let's read Psalm 22:16 and John 19:37.
c3-jhn-0014: John tells what happened at the cross so the Scripture would be fulfilled, and Isaiah says all we like sheep have gone astray. Let's dig into John 19:33 and Isaiah 53:6.
c3-psa-0018: The psalmist pours out how low he has been brought, and Isaiah speaks of the Servant who shall justify many. Let's read Psalm 22:6 and Isaiah 53:11.
c3-mic-0009: Micah speaks of One who will stand when the Assyrian comes, and the psalmist recalls how the fathers trusted God. Let's read Micah 5:5 and Psalm 22:4.
c3-mat-0015: Wise men came seeking the King, and Herod gathered the chief priests and scribes. Let's turn to Matthew 2:4 and Isaiah 53:1.
c2-isa-0026: Isaiah 60 opens with good news for Zion. Let's read Isaiah 60:1.
c2-isa-0027: Isaiah speaks of the foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD. Let's read Isaiah 56:3 and 5.
c3-isa-0020: The LORD describes the kind of fast He has chosen. Let's look closely at Isaiah 58:6 and 9.
c3-isa-0021: The LORD held out His welcome to a nation that had not sought Him. Let's read Isaiah 65:1 and 5.
c3-isa-0022: Isaiah says the LORD's servants shall sing for joy of heart. Let's open Isaiah 65:14 and 66:1.
c3-isa-0023: Isaiah calls everyone to keep justice and do righteousness. Let's read Isaiah 56:1 and 58:10.
c3-isa-0024: Isaiah speaks of eunuchs who keep the LORD's Sabbaths, and of a day of lasting peace for Zion. Let's go to Isaiah 56:4 and 60:18.
c3-isa-0025: The LORD looks on the one who is poor and of a contrite spirit. Let's read Isaiah 58:14 and 66:2.
c3-isa-0026: Isaiah speaks of a new creation that will remain before the LORD. Let's check Isaiah 60:11 and 66:22.
c3-isa-0027: Isaiah says a woman gave birth before she was in labor, and he also speaks of Sharon. Let's read Isaiah 65:10 and 66:7.
c2-ezk-0015: Ezekiel is brought to the gateway, where a man stands waiting. Let's read Ezekiel 40:3.
c2-ezk-0016: Ezekiel is told to look, to hear, and to fix his mind on everything he is shown. Let's look at Ezekiel 40:1 and 4 together.
c3-ezk-0009: The LORD tells Ezekiel to describe the temple to the house of Israel. Let's read Ezekiel 43:10 and 12.
c3-ezk-0010: Ezekiel is led back to the outer threshold that faces east. Let's turn to Ezekiel 44:1 and 17.
c3-ezk-0011: The land is promised to Israel as an inheritance, sworn to their fathers. Let's read Ezekiel 47:14 and 48:30.
c3-ezk-0012: Ezekiel is set on a very high mountain, and later he is told to make known the design of the temple. Let's read Ezekiel 40:2 and 43:11.
c3-ezk-0013: Ezekiel hears the LORD speaking from the temple, and the priests receive rules for their linen clothing. Let's dig into Ezekiel 43:6 and 44:18.
c3-ezk-0014: The priests are given a teaching charge, and a district is set apart for the LORD. Let's read Ezekiel 44:23 and 48:8.
c3-ezk-0015: The land is divided among the tribes of Israel, and the city is given a title forever after. Let's read Ezekiel 47:21 and 48:35.
c3-ezk-0016: Ezekiel is brought toward the east, and later the city's northward openings are called after tribes of Israel. Let's look closely at Ezekiel 43:1 and 48:31.
